question: Two resistors, A(10 Ω) and B (20 Ω), are connected in parallel. The combination is connected to a 6 V battery. The currents in A and B are respectively _______.
solution:
The correct answer is** 0.6 A and 0.3 A**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance in parallel combination**

 
 
• Three resistors connected in parallel to a battery of** voltage V** are depicted in the figure below. In this type of connection, the resistors are typically connected on parallel wires that originate from a common point.
 
• The voltage that **flows** through each resistor is the same in this instance. The equivalent resistance of the three resistances is depicted in the figure on the right.
 
• The equation for the relationship between voltage and current is,** V=IR**

 It can be rewritten as, I=V/R

 The voltages across individual resistors will be, I₁ = V/R₁, I2 = V/R₂, I3 = V/R₃

 The sum of the **current flowing** through each resistance will be, I= I₁+I₂+I₃

 By substituting individual voltages for the expressions, I = V/R₁ + V/R₂ + V/R₃

 Let the **equivalent capacitance** be R, V/R = V/R₁ +V/R₂ + V/R₃
 
• The relation becomes, when the above equation is simplified.

 **1/R= 1/R₁+ 1/R₂+ 1/R₃​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calculations**

 
 
• Two resistors,** A=10 Ω and B=20 Ω**, are connected in parallel

 Voltage= 6V

 We know, V=IR, I=V/R

 **I₁**= 6/10= 3/5= **0.6A**

 **I₂**= 6/20= 3/10=** 0.3A**
